faq.question: Do I need to come to the office in person to start a case?
faq.answer: No. The first consultation can take place by phone or in an online meeting. After the consultation, we submit your application together — either at our office or online through screen sharing.

faq.question: How long does a residence card procedure take?
faq.answer: It depends on the office and the type of case. Whenever your case is delayed, we take steps to speed up the proceedings, and where it is essential we also file a complaint with the court.

faq.question: What happens if my legal stay expires while the case is pending?
faq.answer: Filing a complete application before your legal stay ends usually entitles you to remain in Poland for the duration of the proceedings — confirmed by the relevant stamp in your passport. We check this individually for every case.

faq.question: Do you handle cases outside Warsaw?
faq.answer: We have offices in Warsaw, Łódź and Łowicz, but we help clients across the whole of Poland. Since applications can be submitted online, we also assist you with fingerprint appointments in your own city.

faq.question: How much does it cost to have you handle a case?
faq.answer: The cost depends on the type of procedure and how complex it is. We give a quote after the initial conversation, once we know the scope of work — not before.

karta-pobytu-czasowego.title: Temporary residence card
karta-pobytu-czasowego.summary: Temporary residence permit — work, study, staying with family, or another basis.
karta-pobytu-czasowego.intro: A temporary residence permit is the most common way to legalize a stay in Poland. The application is filed in person at the voivodeship office responsible for the place of stay, no later than the last day of legal stay.

Students and doctoral candidates
Family members of someone living in Poland
People running a business
documents: A completed application and four photographs
A valid travel document (passport) with a copy of every page
Documents confirming the purpose of stay (contract, university certificate, marriage certificate)
Proof of health insurance
Documents confirming a stable source of income
Proof of address
help: We work out the correct legal basis for the application and check whether the deadline still holds
We assemble and verify the documents before filing
We draft the justification for the application
We respond to office requests to complete missing information
We represent you in the proceedings under a power of attorney

pobyt-staly.title: Permanent residence and long-term EU resident status
pobyt-staly.summary: An indefinite permit for holders of the Pole's Card, spouses of Polish citizens, and after years of legal stay.
pobyt-staly.intro: A permanent residence permit is issued for an indefinite period, though the residence card itself must be renewed every ten years. Long-term EU resident status is a separate procedure, available after an uninterrupted stay in Poland.
who: Holders of the Pole's Card
Spouses of Polish citizens, after the required period of marriage and residence
Children of Polish citizens or of people with a permanent residence permit
People after the required period of uninterrupted legal stay
documents: A completed application and four photographs
A valid travel document with a copy
Documents confirming the basis for applying for the permit
Documents confirming an uninterrupted stay in Poland
For EU resident status: proof of Polish language knowledge, stable income and insurance
help: We check whether the period of stay counts as uninterrupted
We choose whichever procedure is more advantageous for your situation
We assemble documentation confirming your residence history
We handle correspondence with the office

zezwolenie-na-prace.summary: Type A and C permits, declarations of entrusting work, seasonal work — for both employee and employer.
zezwolenie-na-prace.intro: It is the employer, not the foreign national, who applies for a work permit. We help both sides: the employee to check that their work is legal, and the employer to run the procedure without formal errors.

zaproszenie-dla-rodziny.title: Invitation for family
zaproszenie-dla-rodziny.summary: Registering an invitation in the register of invitations — a document family members need for a visa application.
zaproszenie-dla-rodziny.intro: An invitation registered by the voivode confirms that the host will provide accommodation and cover the costs of stay for the invited person. It is one of the documents submitted with a visa application.

wymiana-prawa-jazdy.title: Driving licence exchange
wymiana-prawa-jazdy.summary: Exchanging a foreign driving licence for a Polish one, without retaking a course where possible.
wymiana-prawa-jazdy.intro: A foreign driving licence can be exchanged for a Polish one if it was issued by a country that is party to the relevant convention. In some cases a theory exam is required; in others the exchange happens without one.

pesel-i-meldunek.intro: A PESEL number and address registration open access to most official matters: tax settlements, registering with a doctor, setting up a Trusted Profile. Both are handled at the district office.

profil-zaufany.intro: A Trusted Profile lets you handle official matters online and sign applications electronically. Setting it up requires a PESEL number and identity confirmation at a confirmation point or through Polish online banking.

about.title: About the firm
paragraphs: Residence cases are rarely just a formality. Behind every application is a job, a home, a child's school, or a deadline that starts running at the worst possible moment. That's why the first conversation is about the situation, not the form.

We have offices in Warsaw, Łódź and Łowicz and help clients across the whole of Poland. We deal with legalizing residence and work, as well as the related matters that make everyday life in Poland harder without them: a PESEL number, address registration, driving licence exchange, or a Trusted Profile.
Clients talk to us in the languages they actually know. We handle cases in English, Polish, Russian, Hindi, Bengali and Spanish.

privacy.title: Privacy and cookie policy
privacy.metaDescription: How MCH Immigration Law Firm processes personal data and uses cookies, in line with the GDPR.
privacy.intro: This policy explains how we collect and use personal data when you visit this website, contact us or use our services, and how we use cookies. It is provided under Articles 13 and 14 of the General Data Protection Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (GDPR).

administrator.heading: Data controller
administrator.body: The controller of your personal data is {entity}, {street}, {postcode} {city}, Poland, NIP {nip}, REGON {regon}. For any matter relating to your personal data, including exercising your rights, contact us at {email}.

sections.heading: What data we process
paragraphs: Depending on how you interact with us, we process:
items: Contact form: your full name, email address, phone number (optional), the type of case and the content of your message.
Booking a consultation: your name, email address, phone number and the chosen time, collected through Google Calendar appointment scheduling.
Phone and email correspondence: your contact details and the information you share with us.
Handling your case: identity and residence documents and other information needed to represent you before public authorities — including, where the case requires it, data about family members.
Technical data: IP address, browser type, the date and time of the visit and the pages requested, recorded automatically in server logs by our hosting provider.

sections.heading: Purposes and legal bases
paragraphs: We process personal data only where the GDPR gives us a legal basis:
items: Responding to your enquiry and scheduling a consultation — your consent (Art. 6(1)(a) GDPR) and steps taken at your request before entering into a contract (Art. 6(1)(b)).
Providing legal assistance and representing you in proceedings — performance of a contract (Art. 6(1)(b)).
Meeting legal obligations, such as accounting and tax record-keeping — legal obligation (Art. 6(1)(c)).
Keeping the website secure, preventing spam and abuse, and establishing or defending legal claims — our legitimate interests (Art. 6(1)(f)).
Loading embedded third-party content that sets cookies — your consent (Art. 6(1)(a)), given through the cookie banner.

sections.heading: How long we keep data
items: Enquiries that do not lead to an engagement: up to 12 months from our last contact.
Client files: for the duration of the engagement and then until any claims become time-barred, generally 6 years after the case ends.
Accounting documents: 5 years from the end of the calendar year in which the tax obligation arose, as required by Polish law.
Data processed on the basis of consent: until you withdraw your consent, or earlier if the purpose has been achieved.
Server logs: for a short period set by our hosting provider, normally no longer than 30 days.

sections.heading: Who receives your data
paragraphs: We do not sell personal data. We share it only with entities that help us run the website and our practice, under data processing agreements, or where the law requires it:
items: Vercel Inc. — website hosting.
Our email service provider — delivery of messages sent through the contact form and of email correspondence.
Google Ireland Ltd and Google LLC — the appointment booking calendar.
Cloudflare, Inc. — protection of the contact form against spam and bots (Turnstile), where enabled.
IT, accounting and legal service providers, to the extent necessary.
Public authorities, such as voivodeship offices, courts and the Office for Foreigners, when we file applications on your behalf or where the law requires it.

sections.heading: Transfers outside the European Economic Area
paragraphs: Some of our providers (Vercel, Google, Cloudflare) are based in the United States or may process data there. Such transfers rely on the European Commission's adequacy decision for the EU–US Data Privacy Framework, for providers certified under it, or on Standard Contractual Clauses approved by the European Commission. You can ask us for a copy of the applicable safeguards.

sections.heading: Your rights
paragraphs: Under the GDPR you have the right to:
items: access your data and receive a copy of it (Art. 15);
have inaccurate data rectified (Art. 16);
have your data erased (Art. 17);
restrict processing (Art. 18);
data portability (Art. 20);
object to processing based on our legitimate interests (Art. 21);
withdraw your consent at any time, without affecting the lawfulness of processing carried out before the withdrawal (Art. 7(3));
lodge a complaint with the supervisory authority — the President of the Personal Data Protection Office (Prezes Urzędu Ochrony Danych Osobowych), ul. Stawki 2, 00-193 Warszawa, uodo.gov.pl.

sections.heading: Is providing data required?
paragraphs: Providing data is voluntary, but without your contact details we cannot reply to your enquiry, and without the documents a procedure requires we cannot represent you in it.

sections.heading: Automated decision-making
paragraphs: We do not make decisions based solely on automated processing, including profiling, that produce legal effects for you.

cookies.heading: Cookies
paragraphs: Cookies are small text files that a website stores on your device. We use them in line with Article 5(3) of the ePrivacy Directive (2002/58/EC), as implemented in Polish law, and the GDPR.

Strictly necessary cookies are needed for the site to work and do not require consent. Any other cookies are used only after you agree to them in the cookie banner. You can change or withdraw your choice at any time using the “Cookie settings” link at the bottom of every page, or delete cookies in your browser settings.
